messages:
maria: Quick heads up — onboarding Celestia-lite (4B) int4 conversion shows a quality regression on summarization and a perplexity spike for long contexts (>1024). I suspect a rotary scale mismatch plus tokenizer id shadowing.

simon: numbers? where's the diff vs fp16?

maria: quick eval snapshot (harness run id=cel-2026-03-21-02):
```
fp16  - summarization R1: 0.42, ppl@1k: 18.4
int4  - summarization R1: 0.33, ppl@1k: 26.7
```
Also noticed samples with coherent prefix collapse after ~600 tokens.

aya: can you paste the exported model/convert config and tokenizer diff?

maria: model convert snippet pasted below — converter left rotary_scale=1.0 (exporter default) while other variants we use have scale ~0.707.
```
# convert.yaml
model_name: celestia-lite-4b
rotary_dim: 64
rotary_scale: 1.0  # from converter v0.3.2
head_dim: 64
qconfig: symmetric-perchannel-int4
```
Tokenizer diff: our internal normalizer remapped BOS from 1 -> 2 and added a soft-hyphen token that collides with an existing sentinel id in the model vocab -> possible "token shadowing".

jonathan: did you try nf4 or a different quant scheme? nf4 can sometimes preserve distributional tails better. Also which runtime kernel did you use for rotary?

maria: current run used symmetric-int4 + continuous batching kernel (xform-qconv). Not yet tried nf4. Rotary implementation was the standard fused sincos with headwise multiply — no per-head scale adjustment.

build-bot: perf job queued: cel-2026-03-21-02-nf4-rotfix (id: build-9812). Estimated ~45m.

simon: also recommend a parity test: run fp16 but apply the new tokenizer mapping (simulate export mapping) — if gap reduces it's tokenizer-shadowing, else it's rotary/kv-indexing.

aya: +1. Also add kv-cache index parity: off-by-one rotary indexing will show prefix drift but stable short-context behavior.

maria: action checklist I'm running/queuing now:
- convert->nf4 with rotary_scale=0.707 and run eval harness (200 long-doc summarizations)
- run fp16 with new tokenizer mapping to check vocab-shadowing parity
- kv-cache index parity check (first 2048 steps) to detect indexing offset
- capture sample traces for the fused rotary kernel and compare per-head norms

jonathan: I can take the nf4 converter patch and the kernel traces. Will fork convert and add a --rotary-scale flag. Ping me when you want me to land.

maria: thanks — will add test artifacts to the thread once build finishes. dropping logs/artifacts here when available. :rocket:

simon: thanks, this matches a few symptoms we saw with Gemma->Qwen conversions last quarter. Good catch on tokenizer shadowing — that one hides in plain sight. :eyes:
